Phonon Force Data Preparation

This tutorial prepares FORCE_SETS for QTrans using the finite-displacement workflow in Phonopy: generate displaced supercells, calculate their atomic forces with a DFT code, and collect the forces into a Phonopy dataset. Bulk Al examples are provided for VASP and ABACUS.

The VASP force calculations are stored in tutorials/Al/openmx/phonopy/ because they supply phonons for the OpenMX transport examples. The electronic Hamiltonian and phonon forces do not have to come from the same DFT code, but their structures, atom ordering, and physical settings must be consistent.

Important

QTrans reads FORCE_SETS using Phonopy’s default VASP convention: displacements in angstrom and forces in eV/angstrom. A FORCE_SETS file does not identify its units. Generating it successfully with Phonopy does not guarantee that its units are suitable for QTrans.

In particular, Phonopy’s ABACUS interface writes displacements in bohr and forces in eV/angstrom. Convert the displacement vectors before supplying that dataset to QTrans; leave the force values unchanged.

VASP force calculations

For DFT parameter definitions and execution details, consult the VASP documentation and the Phonopy VASP interface. The supplied supercells/INCAR, KPOINTS, and potential inputs provide an example setup; converge the force accuracy for your own calculation.

Step 1. Generate displaced supercells

From the tutorial repository root, enter the example directory and generate a 3 x 3 x 3 supercell from the primitive-cell POSCAR:

cd tutorials/Al/openmx/phonopy/
phonopy -d --dim="3 3 3"

VASP is Phonopy’s default interface, so no calculator flag is needed. The reference files include SPOSCAR (the undisplaced supercell), POSCAR-001 (a displaced supercell), and phonopy_disp.yaml (the structure and displacement information). This Al example has 27 atoms in the supercell and one symmetry-independent displacement. Other materials can require several POSCAR-xxx files.

Keep phonopy_disp.yaml in the working directory. For this example, copy the displaced structure into the prepared force-calculation directory:

cp POSCAR-001 supercells/POSCAR

Step 2. Calculate forces

Run a static, self-consistent VASP calculation in supercells/ with the displaced atomic positions fixed. Do not relax the displaced structure. For example, using your VASP executable and MPI configuration:

cd supercells/
mpirun -np 8 vasp_std > vasp.out
cd ..

The supplied reference INCAR uses ENCUT = 500 eV, EDIFF = 1E-08, IBRION = -1, and NSW = 0. Adjust parallel settings and potential paths for your installation. Confirm electronic convergence and the presence of atomic forces in vasprun.xml. If several displacements are generated, calculate each in its own directory with consistent DFT settings.

Step 3. Collect forces

From the directory containing phonopy_disp.yaml, run:

phonopy -f ./supercells/vasprun.xml

For several displacement directories, pass all output files in the same order as the displaced structures. With appropriately named directories, the usual command is:

phonopy -f ./*/vasprun.xml

This generates FORCE_SETS. VASP-interface displacements are already in angstrom and forces in eV/angstrom, so no unit conversion is needed. Reference inputs and outputs are in ref/. After checking the result, copy it to the data directory used by the Al examples:

cp FORCE_SETS ../data/FORCE_SETS

ABACUS force calculations

For DFT parameters and execution details, consult the ABACUS documentation and the Phonopy ABACUS interface. The example is in tutorials/Al/abacus/phonopy/; reference structures, force outputs, and the conversion script are in ref/.

Step 1. Generate displaced supercells

From the tutorial repository root, run:

cd tutorials/Al/abacus/phonopy/
phonopy --abacus -d --dim="3 3 3"

Here --abacus selects the ABACUS interface and reads the primitive-cell STRU. Phonopy generates STRU-001 and phonopy_disp.yaml for this 27-atom Al supercell. Copy the displaced structure into the prepared calculation directory:

cp STRU-001 supercells/STRU

Step 2. Calculate forces

Use a static SCF calculation (calculation scf) and enable force output with cal_force 1 in supercells/INPUT. The supplied example uses basis_type lcao, ecutwfc 100 Ry, and scf_thr 1e-9. Update pseudo_dir, orbital_dir, and the referenced potential and orbital files for your installation. Keep the displaced atomic positions fixed.

cd supercells/
mpirun -np 8 abacus > abacus.out
cd ..

For suffix Al, the force output needed by Phonopy is supercells/OUT.Al/running_scf.log. Check SCF convergence and force output before collecting the dataset. Repeat for every displaced supercell if more than one is generated.

Step 3. Collect forces and convert units

From the directory containing the ABACUS phonopy_disp.yaml, run:

phonopy --abacus -f ./supercells/OUT.Al/running_scf.log

For multiple displacements, supply all corresponding running_scf.log files in displacement order. The resulting FORCE_SETS uses the ABACUS interface convention:

Quantity

Original ABACUS-interface dataset

Dataset for QTrans

Displacement

bohr

angstrom (multiply by approximately 0.529177)

Force

eV/angstrom

eV/angstrom (unchanged)

The QTrans script ref/phonon_convert.py converts this type-1 finite-displacement dataset using the unit factor from the installed Phonopy version:

python ref/phonon_convert.py --calculator abacus --input FORCE_SETS --output FORCE_SETS_converted
cp FORCE_SETS_converted ../data/FORCE_SETS

The script preserves the original file and refuses to overwrite an existing output. If FORCE_SETS_converted already exists, choose a new output filename. Convert the original ABACUS-interface file only once; its units cannot be inferred automatically from its contents.

In the supplied reference, the first displacement changes from [-0.0141421356237309, 0, 0.0141421356237309] bohr to approximately [-0.007483696, 0, 0.007483696] angstrom. The force components remain unchanged. Last digits can differ slightly with the physical constants used by different Phonopy versions.

Keep the original FORCE_SETS together with the ABACUS phonopy_disp.yaml for calculations through Phonopy’s ABACUS interface. The converted copy is for QTrans’s VASP-unit reader; do not combine it with ABACUS-unit displacements in a subsequent Phonopy calculation.

Use the force data in QTrans

The Al calculation inputs read ../data/FORCE_SETS together with ../data/Al-pri.vasp and phonon.supercell_matrix set to a diagonal 3 x 3 x 3 supercell. Use the matching primitive structure in angstrom, with the same cell orientation and atom ordering as the force calculation. The phonon supercell size is independent of the supercell used to prepare EPC gradients.

See Dispersion of Quasiparticle and DOS of Quasiparticle for complete QTrans inputs that calculate phonon dispersions and DOS. The Workflow summarizes the input conventions for other interfaces. Check the units of the actual Phonopy interface before reusing force data from another DFT code; do not apply the ABACUS conversion indiscriminately.
